commentary:
This is the confirm pass over the two walks' own additions, and the three things it found are all one shape: a pointer moved in the OWNING text and the cascade stopped one artifact short. Walk 1 re-pointed A3's middle clause and its cascade reached the body, the design's repair table, the task note and the parity note — but not the proposal's What Changes bullet, which still names the owner the delta left. The older of the two proposal defects is the same shape a walk earlier: the in-context proposal walk moved A4's pointer from the maturity requirement to the grammar requirement in the delta, the design row and the task, and the proposal's two sentences about A4 were never touched — six passes have now read past them. The decision record D-rc16-2 lags for the same reason: its owner list was written when four owners existed. None of the three touches a delta, the body, a test or a baseline; the deltas, the body and the generated skill agree with each other everywhere I compared them.

Probed and re-run rather than trusted: `npm test` on the walked tree (100 files, 2376 passed); `orbit validate rc16-retirement-sweep --strict` (valid); `orbit fingerprint --check` (6 verified); `orbit validate --sources` (stages 25, rulings 14, capabilities 21, schema-version 4 — unmoved after the design gained a fenced block and a paragraph); body line 610 against delta line 74 after unescaping (IDENTICAL) and the design's A3 row quote against the same line (IDENTICAL); the eleven quoted sentences over the three deltas and the body (0/0/0/0) and the widened grep over the body (0); the regenerated `.claude/skills/orbit-explore/SKILL.md` for both walk-1 sentences (present once each); and a grep for every 'maturity' mention across proposal, design and tasks, which is how the two proposal sentences surfaced. Body line 606 was checked deliberately because it ALSO points the Concluded rung at the maturity requirement: that sentence is about the EMIT's recorded `next_recommended`, which the maturity requirement does own (the rung's text), so it is correct and distinct from line 610's row-render claim — the distinction walk 1 drew holds.

Passes 4 and 5 were skipped: `orbit/lenses/` is absent, per the body's degradation rule; the fresh pass ran substitutes for both and the external covered the adopter perspective, so this pass did not repeat them. Pass 6 ran the audit-drift categories by hand over the change's own artifacts rather than through the skill, to keep one emit on the trail; the project-wide run is exit (3)'s at-archive act and was not pre-empted. Risk texture: the walk-2 fenced grep block inside design.md is the first fenced shell command in a design artifact on this program — `orbit validate --strict` and the source lint read past it cleanly, and nothing parses design.md, so it carries no engine risk; it is worth knowing it is there. The explore.md's superseded D-rc16-2 entry still names the exploration's six-phrase grep as its source — by rule, unchanged history, and I did not raise it.
